extractionRisks: Rhetorical personification can make a polity look like a person
Historical examples must not be flattened into the author's own claims
Religious and natural-law appeals may function as evidence without being presented as neutral fact
The source uses historical spellings such as independance and connexion that should remain verbatim in excerpts
namingConventions: Polities and institutions are usually capitalized
Political doctrines and systems recur as common nouns
Arguments often contrast paired alternatives such as society and government or reconciliation and independence
corpusProfile.structure: Introduction followed by topical essays that define political principles, rebut monarchy and reconciliation, and advance independence and institutional proposals
